title: WIMSE Lab
summary: IETF WIMSE mock: trust domains, Workload Identity Tokens (WIT), Workload Proof Tokens (WPT), and a multi-hop chain where every hop is verified and cryptographically bound.

cards.title: Trust domain
cards.body: The administrative scope for workload identities. Our issuer is authorized for {{cast.trustDomain}} only; a credential naming another domain is refused even when our own key signed it.

cards.title: Workload Identity Token (WIT)
cards.body: A JWT naming the workload ({{cast.witSub}}) with a cnf.jwk confirmation key. A WIT is never bearer: possession of the matching private key must be proven.

cards.title: Workload Proof Token (WPT)
cards.body: A per-request JWT sent as Authorization: WPT <token>. Claims: aud = exact target URI, exp = seconds, jti = replay protection, wth = hash of the WIT, tth = hash of the Txn-Token for {{cast.user}}.

cards.title: Multi-hop chain
cards.body: {{cast.gateway}} → {{cast.orders}} → {{cast.billing}}. Every hop presents WIT + WPT + Txn-Token and every hop is validated.

cards.title: Break it on purpose
cards.body: Wrong audience, swapped user context (tth), swapped workload (wth), expired WIT, rogue trust domain — each shows the exact refusal.
